title: TS-66 Handoff step 2: the container owner entry point and the unprivileged shell
description:
Source: the Pi session handoff spike (PR 474: spikes/pi-handoff, docs/PI_HARNESS.md section 'Spike: handoff to a computer owner', GO in steps) and docs/PI_SESSION_HANDOFF.md. Decision (user): the goal is a Pi session running in the computer container, using Pi's own tools (read, write, edit, bash from @earendil-works/pi-durable/tools), with the session portable between owners. Security gate before production: the container must not hold the model key or broad storage credentials.

computer/host: an owner entry point bundled with esbuild (about 4 MB) that takes over a turn with takeOverTurn (TS-65) inside the container; the model-chosen shell commands run as a different unprivileged uid with a scrubbed environment (the spike found a same-user child could read /proc/PPID/environ; a different uid cannot); image changes (a shell user, no credentials readable by it); run it in the local arm64 container against the moto container over a bridge network (host.docker.internal was unreliable) with the faux provider and measure start to first tool result; a scenario or test proving the shell user cannot read the owner's environment or files. No AWS.
right_now_summary: The team is defining a secure container handoff with an unprivileged shell and no exposed credentials.
